links.reason: 213 is an open revolt by kin (நின்தலை வந்த இருவரை, இளையோர் தோற்பின்) argued as a dilemma: no heir if they fall (செல்வம் யார்க்கு எஞ்சுவை), only பழி if he falls. Kural 889's உட்பகை is a concealed enmity whose sesame-small seed (எட்பக) holds ruin; the poem applies the theme of strife within but does not show the Kural's mechanism, so 'gives the reason' overstates.

The contrast is real: 1151 is a barbed refusal (வல்வரவு வாழ்வார்க்கு உரை), 143 a report of tears (கண்பனி கலுழ்ந்தன; நோகோ யானே). But the poem never says the plea succeeded; that comes only from the colophon's செலவழுங்குவித்தது, so 'the poem shows the second one succeeding' leans on the colophon.

Both refuse to let good fortune and ill shift the mind: 192 வாழ்தல் இனிதுஎன மகிழ்ந்தன்றும் இலமே ... இன்னாது என்றலும் இலமே, 379 நன்றாங்கால் ... அன்றாங்கால் அல்லற் படுவது எவன். Both ground it in an order beyond the self (முறைவழிப் படூஉம் / the ஊழ் chapter), and the raft on the flood is a concrete image the couplet lacks.

228 does not use the urn as a measure the king meets; it says no urn could hold him (இருநிலம் திகிரியா, பெருமலை மண்ணா), so greatness escapes the rite there too, just as 231 says the pyre's size cannot touch fame (புகழ் மாயலவே). The two poems agree; the claimed opposition of 'measure' and 'escape' is imposed.

The verbal echo is exact: 141 'எத்துணை ஆயினும் ஈதல் நன்று' ... மறுமை நோக்கின்றோ அன்றே and 222 மேலுலகம் இல்லெனினும் ஈதலே நன்று. 141 adds what the couplet leaves out, the positive motive (பிறர் வறுமை நோக்கின்று), proved by the gift to a peacock that can neither wear nor wrap it (உடாஅ போரா ஆகுதல் அறிந்தும்).

The name link is real (உதியஞ் சேரல் / உதியன் சேரலாதன்) and the akam use is stated: the girls rejoice like பாடிச் சென்ற பரிசிலர். But Puram 2 praises feeding the armies in the war (பெருஞ்சோற்று மிகுபதம் வரையாது கொடுத்தோய்), not feeding bards, and Akam 65's epithet is நாடுகண் அகற்றிய; 'feeder of bards' and 'proverbial' go beyond both texts.

Both friends assure the woman with the Moriyar's rock-cut road (மோரியர் ... அறைவாய் / மோரியர் ... குறைத்த அறை) and a promise of return (தங்கலர் / நீடலர்), and 251 does sharpen it with நந்தன் வெறுக்கை எய்தினும். The tie is a shared historical image in two independent poems, which same_image names better than develops.

Same battle, same thurai, and both catalogue the end of drums and armies (முரசு ஒழிந்தனவே / முரசம் ... இருந்துவிளிந் தனவே). But 62 is not a consolation by glory: it opens அமர்மிகல் யாவது? and shows no one left to claim the field and the queens dying, so it counts the cost as 63 does; the split 'glory versus cost' misdescribes 62.

306 does put the prayer for guests first (விருந்து எதிர் பெறுகதில் யானே) before the husband's war, which embodies the Kural's விருந்தோம்பி வேளாண்மை. 'A prayer before it was a maxim' is a chronology flourish and 'ranked first' rests on word order in a verse with a gap at line 6.
links.text_issue: line 6 is mostly lost (ஒ .. .. .. வேந்தனொடு), so what she asks for her husband is incomplete

links.reason: The contrast is real: 16 boasts that fields that knew only sugarcane (கரும்பு அல்லது காடு அறியா) became waste, while 18 says உண்டி கொடுத்தோர் உயிர்கொடுத்தோரே. But 18 never limits its counsel to the king's own land, so the claim that the anthology 'shows' the duty applied only at home is the proposer's reconciliation, not something either poem says.

The wording matches: வந்துவினை முடித்தனன் வேந்தனும் ... இன்துயில் பெறவே and வினைகலந்து வென்றீக வேந்தன் மனைகலந்து மாலை அயர்கம் விருந்து. But the couplet is a wish spoken while the king's war is still on (வென்றீக), and 44 is the war finished and the man driving home, so calling the couplet the homecoming formula 'reduced' misses that one waits and the other returns.

Both are Paranar's and both cite Anni Minjili's revenge on the Kosar through Thithiyan (196 ஒன்றுமொழிக் கோசர்க் கொன்று ... அன்னி மிஞிலியின் இயலும்; 262 அவர் இன்உயிர் செகுப்பக் கண்டு சினம் மாறிய அன்னி மிஞிலி போல). The opposite uses (the rival's pride, the lover's joy) are accurately described, but one poem does not develop the other; it is a shared puram figure.

The two Kapilar poems are rightly paired by Parambu and counting from the hill (பொலம் படைக் கலிமா எண்ணுவோரே). But 109 already speaks to kings who have come and are besieging (மூவிரும் முற்றினும்), so 'the kings did come' is not something it left out, and 109 never promised the fort safe outright: it named the bards' road by which it could be had.
links.text_issue: the marker notes a line missing after line 9 and an ambiguous line 14 (வியன்மலை அற்றே)

links.reason: Both Mamulanar poems name Cheralathan by the same deeds (முந்நீர் ஓட்டிக் கடம்புஅறுத்து / மால்கடல் ஓட்டிக் கடம்பு அறுத்து) and use them for different measures: the hoard of tribute (பணிதிறை தந்த ... நிதியத்து அன்ன) for wealth he would not stay for, and the drum (பண்ணமை முரசின் கண் அதிர்ந்தன்ன) for the gossip. The note says what each akam poet does with the name.

364 draws enjoyment from the nearness of the burning ground (உண்டும் தின்றும் ... மகிழ்கம் ... தாழிய பெருங்காடு எய்திய ஞான்றே), while Naladiyar 16 calls the joy enjoyed in the presence of slaughter (மறிகுளகு உண்டன்ன மன்னா மகிழ்ச்சி) foreign to the wise. On the plain reading the feast is the lamb's pleasure, so the tension is real and the teaches sentence states it precisely.

Kural 87 measures the fruit (பயன்) of hospitality by the guest's worth (விருந்தின் துணைத்துணை வேள்விப் பயன்); it says nothing about sizing the gift to the guest. The 'opposite scale' therefore depends on reading the couplet as a rule for how much to give, which is not what துணை here measures; 387's என் சிறுமையின் இழித்து நோக்கான் is real but does not answer it.

Kazhuvul's Kamur is named in both (ஈர்எழு வேளிர் ... எறிந்த கழுவுள் காமூர் போல; மாவண் கழுவுள் காமூர் ஆங்கண் பூதம் தந்த ... வேங்கை), once as a besieged town for the shaken heart and once as the grove whose vengai scents her hair. The note says what each akam poet does with the name, and the teaches sentence claims no more than the two uses show.

Both rebuke the heart midway that now wants to turn back, and both name the stake through laughter: 21 மனைநகப் பல்வேறு வெறுக்கை தருகம், 33 எய்துவை அல்லையோ பிறர்நகு பொருளோ. 33 also concedes that never leaving would have been better (பிரியாய் ஆயின் நன்றுமற் றில்ல), so the pair shows two sides of one argument.

Kural 759 is statecraft: wealth as the steel that cuts the enemy's pride (செறுநர் செருக்கறுக்கும் எஃகு). Akam 239 is a man's memory of a girl's question (நீட்டுவிர் அல்லிரோ) as he leaves for wealth; the only common ground is the large topic of seeking wealth, and the 'paid for by someone left behind' sentence is that topic restated.

The heart-and-face pair is distinctive and shared: 207 rejects a gift that is அகம்நக வாரா முகன்அழி, 786 says முகநக நட்பது நட்பன்று ... அகநக நட்பது நட்பு. In both the heart's gladness is the real test, and the pairing shows the same measure in patronage and in friendship.

Both have the body tell of a departure before words do: 1157's slipping bangles (இறைஇறவா நின்ற வளை ... தூற்றா) and 161's tears (பல்லிதழ் உண்கண் பரந்தன பனியே). The signs differ, though (wasting after he has gone against tears at a guessed plan, கேட்டனள் கொல்லோ), and the link rests on the shared situation more than on one sharpening the other.

165's giver who has lost his land offers his head (நாடுஇழந் ததனினும் நனிஇன்னாது ... வாள்தந் தனனே, தலை எனக்கு ஈய) and 160's Kumanan flings away gold vessels at Muthiram (பொலங்கலம் எளிதினின் வீசி). But 165 names no one, and only the colophon makes the two the same man. The 'same habit tested after the land is gone' depends on that identity.
links.text_issue: 160 has four variant lines; at line 10 கோடின்றாக against கேடின்றாக bears on 'may not fail'

links.reason: 75 quotes the அருள்/பொருள் opposition of the Kural's kind ('அருள் அன்று ஆக, ஆள்வினை, ஆடவர் பொருள்') and refutes it with a thing of this world that no one can give back (தருநரும் உளரோ இவ் உலகத்தான்). That answers 247's grant of இவ்வுலகம் to wealth directly, so the qualification is specific and accurate.

Fame after death is the shared topic. 282's நாநவில் புலவர் வாய் உளானே is clear, but 235's 'death that is existence' rests on a contested reading (நத்தம் as growth), and the couplet credits வித்தகர் with achieving it themselves. 'Depended on someone to sing it' is laid onto the Kural, not drawn from it.
links.text_issue: 282 line 4 is lost, and the poem has no thinai or thurai

links.reason: 68 points the bard to a giver so open that he will forget other doors (பிறன்கடை மறப்ப நல்குவன்), and 1053 grants a grace to asking before கரப்பிலா நெஞ்சின் கடனறிவார். The fit is real but general; 'allows asking only before the right giver' and 'solving the Kural's problem' overstate a couplet that only says such asking has a beauty.

The image is shared and distinctive: a laugh after an elephant kill (பெயர்புறம் நகுமே; மெய்வேல் பறியா நகும்). But the Kural's laugh is not scorn turned on the self; the hero laughs because he has found a spear to use. 'Moving the scorn of fear from the enemy to the self' misreads 774.

The link of hearing about a son (சான்றோன் எனக்கேட்ட தாய்; நின்னுரை செல்லும் ஆயின்) is real. But 254's mother does not take her joy from hearing him praised: she praises him herself every day (நாளும் ஆனாது புகழும் அன்னை). The teaches sentence misdescribes the poem.

Both mothers picture the eloped daughter's new home: 15 wishes the town may be welcoming (வறுங்கை வம்பலர் தாங்கும் பண்பின் ... மூதூர்) and 369 fears a poor one-cow hut (ஓர்ஆ யாத்த ஒருதூண் முன்றில்). Both also liken the home left behind to a famous fort or city (நன்னன் பாழி; உறந்தை). The teaches sentence is accurate, but it describes a shared motif, not one poem limiting the other.

Shared topic only: the fall of a lord. The 'qualification' is an argument from silence in a five-line lament (எந்தையும் இலமே) that gives no cause, and calling the father a blameless famous giver brings in the colophon (பாரி மகளிர்), since the poem says nothing of his giving or his innocence.

66 is a concrete case of the Kural's rule (இளிவரின் வாழாத மானம் உடையார் ஒளிதொழுது ஏத்தும் உலகு): a king ashamed of a wound on his back (புறப்புண் நாணி) dies facing north and reaches மிகப் புகழ் உலகம. The poet also tells the victor to his face நின்னினும் நல்லன் அன்றே. The pair shows the praise in public, as the teaches sentence says.

The verbal tie is exact: 377 இசைபடப் பெய்தல் ஆற்றுவோரே, 231 ஈதல் இசைபட வாழ்தல். 377 shows such givers must spend nights as strangers in a ruined hall (வம்பலர் ஆகியும் கழிப மன்ற) thinking of their women. That is a real condition on the Kural's single profit.

The deer family is shared (சிறுமறி தழீஇய ... மடப்பிணை ... இரலை; மறியுடை மடப்பிணை தழீஇ ... இரலை). But both poems are mullai with the same uri, and in 314 the scene goes with her near-despair before he comes (இந்நிலை வாரார் ஆயின்), not with fulfilment. 'Fixed by the uri' and 'fulfilment when he returns' both misstate it.

Pittan is named in both, and the akam use (tears like the நீலம் of his hill pool) is stated. But the epithets are not one formula: 143 has நசையின் வாழ்நர்க்கு நன்கலஞ் சுரக்கும் and 170 has நசைவர்க்கு மென்மை; only the common word நசை is shared, so 'passing whole' overstates.

The same word carries opposite verdicts: 194 இன்னாது அம்ம இவ் வுலகம், blaming the maker (படைத்தோன் ... பண்பிலாளன்), against 192 இன்னா தென்றலும் இலமே. 194's last line (இனிய காண்க) softens it, but the judgment itself is incompatible, as the note says.

Both mothers of an eloped girl recall coaxing her with milk (பால்பெய் வள்ளம் ... 'நுந்தை பாடும் உண்'; தேம்கலந்து அளைஇய தீம்பால் ஏந்தி ... மறுத்த) and set it against the waterless or brackish road (நீர்இல் நீள்இடை; தெண்கண் உவரிக் குறைக்குட முகவை). The image is distinctive and used the same way in both.

The shared toddy is real (சிறியகட் பெறினே எமக்கீயும்; நார்அரி சிறுகலத்து உகுப்பவும்). But 232 gives its own reason for disbelief: he would not take even a whole mountain country (நாடு உடன் கொடுப்பவும் கொள்ளாதோனே). The role-reversal 'which is why' is not in the poem, and 232 does not even say that she pours.

கழல்தொடி with the Athiyar name (கழல்தொடி தடக்கை ... அதியர் கோமான்; நசைபிழைப்பு அறியாக் கழல்தொடி அதிகன்) is a real tie, and the note is careful about identity. But கழல்தொடி is a common heroic epithet, and in 162 the hill serves the comparison of the girl to its goddesses (சூரா மகளிரிற் பெறற்கு அரியோள்), so the link is thin.

Pari, and Kapilar with him, are in both: 78 வாய்மொழிக் கபிலன் சூழ ... வேந்தர் ஓட்டிய ... கைவண் பாரி, and 201 Kapilar giving the daughters away (யானே தந்தை தோழன்). The contrast of the hero at his height against the aftermath holds for this pair. The tie is a shared name, not an image, and the generalisation about akam and puram rests on one pair.

Avvai builds both portraits by the same device, one object and its other state joined by மற்றதன்: the elephant and its musth (மற்றதன் துன்னருங் கடாஅம்), and the fire-stick and its blaze (மற்றதன் கான்றுபடு கனைஎரி). That supports the teaches claim that the double nature, not any single image, is her settled view of Anji.

The refrain is exact and striking: வருந்தா யாணர்த்து; நந்துங் கொல்லோ and மெந்தினை யாணர்த்து; நந்துங் கொல்லோ, each followed by the land as the patron's (நாடே). But 'shows the poems were made as a set' claims a fact of composition that a shared formula in one poet's laments does not prove.

Both Paranar poems tell Aay Eyinan's death against Minjili at Paazhi (இகலடு கற்பின் மிஞிலியொடு தாக்கித் தன்னுயிர் கொடுத்தனன்; மிஞிலியொடு ... வீழ்ந்தென). 396 adds the cause, the 'அஞ்சல்' promised to those Nannan drove from Punnadu, and sets it against a lover who broke a vow made before a god (கடவுள் முன்னர்த் தேற்றி).

The staff image is shared (தொடித்தலை விழுத்தண்டு ஊன்றி; கோல்ஊன்றி இன்னாங்கு எழுந்திருப்பார்). Naladiyar 11 condemns those who delighted in youth (மன்னா இளமை மகிழ்ந்தாரே), and 243's speaker is exactly such a man, who instead longs for his கல்லா இளமை (அளிதோ தானே). The incompatibility is direct.

The ploughing figure ties them (வாளேர் உழவ in 368; தேர்ஏ ராக ... வித்தி ... பொலிகளம் in 369), and both ask for a முகவை. But 368 has no harvest structure; its request follows a field with no booty left (முகவை இன்மையின்). 'In both the request stands where the labourer's share would' holds only for 369.

Both tie அருள் to escape from hell: 5 warns against those who cast off அருளும் அன்பும் and take நீங்கா நிரயம், and 243 says அருள்சேர்ந்த நெஞ்சினார்க்கு இல்லை இருள்சேர்ந்த இன்னா உலகம் புகல். 5 turns this into government (காவல் குழவி கொள்பவரின் ஓம்புமதி), as the teaches sentence says.

iraicchi.act: the stag and doe lie together in union (காமர் புணர்நிலை), which the chariot's noise could break
iraicchi.sense: The returning man spares the deer's union because he is hurrying to his own, so their togetherness speaks for his longing.

iraicchi.act: the tiger cannot bear its mate's hunger and lies in wait for a boar to feed her
iraicchi.sense: Even the beast stays to provide for its mate, while her man, gone for wealth, has not come back as the season arrived.

poems.note: The tiger is part of the road description; whether its care is meant against the absent man is an inference, though it meets the four conditions.
The ripened millet means the guarding will end, but the poem says the consequence openly, and no second correspondence can be named.

iraicchi.act: the bull elephant cherishes its herd, bringing sprouts and feeding them the fodder they want
iraicchi.sense: The tusker provides for its own, as the man should take her as his own and provide for her by marrying her instead of coming by night.

poems.note: The elephant sits in a clause attached to the storm-night description, so it is a background detail rather than an image the speaker points to.

iraicchi.act: the house dove flies about with its mate
iraicchi.sense: The dove keeps beside its mate while she, without him, watches it and the children and thinks of him.

poems.note: The poem states its own point (மாண்நலம் நுகரும் துணைஉடையோர்க்கே), so the farmers' scene is an open contrast, not a hidden one.

iraicchi.act: the stag holds his doe close and grazes and frisks with her in the evening
iraicchi.sense: Even the deer keep their mates in the rainy evening, which shows how wrong the absent man is not to remember her (மாலையும் உள்ளார்).

ullurai.anchor: செந்நெல் வினைஞர் கட்கொண்டு மறுகும் சாகாடு அளற்றுஉறின் ஆய்கடும்பு அடுக்கும்

poems.note: The pairs (drunk workers to his revelry, a cart sunk in mire to his name sunk in scandal) are an inference from the scene; the situation is stated in lines 9 to 12 and the thurai.
